description_good: README.md describes Tsu Cwico: a Windows debloater that scans installed software, classifies each item Safe/Caution/Critical and removes it with a restore point and registry backup first: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/README.md
interact: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md explain how to get the source and binaries, report bugs (issue form) and contribute: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the pull request process and the checks to run first: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test, UI build, both translations, the safety rules for the catalogue: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
documentation_basics: README.md covers installation (winget, Scoop, installer), usage, the safety model and verification; docs/SAFETY.md documents the classification: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/docs/SAFETY.md
documentation_interface: The CLI (cwico info, scan, plan, ...) and its flags are documented in the README command-line section: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/README.md
sites_https: Project site https://cwico.tsudev.com and the GitHub repository/releases are HTTPS only.
discussion: GitHub Issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/issues
english: Documentation is in English (Vietnamese translation in docs/README.vi.md): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/README.md
maintained: Actively maintained, regular commits in November 2026: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/commits/main
repo_track: Git tracks every change with author and date.
repo_interim: Work in progress is pushed to branches and pull requests between releases.
version_unique: Each release has a unique version and git tag: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/tags
version_semver: Calendar Versioning (YY.M.DD with a build counter), managed by tools/version.py: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md
release_notes: CHANGELOG.md summarises each release; the entry is also shown in the update dialog: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in any release so far.
report_process: Bug reports use GitHub Issues with an issue form: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/issues/new/choose
report_responses: No external bug report has been filed so far; the maintainer reads every issue and acknowledges reports within days.
enhancement_responses: No external enhancement request has been filed so far; the maintainer answers each one.
report_archive: GitHub Issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process: SECURITY.md explains what counts as a vulnerability for this tool and how to report it: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response: No vulnerability report was received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to an acknowledgement within 72 hours.
build: cargo build plus the Tauri bundler; the release workflow builds the installers on GitHub Actions from a tagged commit: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
build_common_tools: cargo, npm and the Tauri CLI.
build_floss_tools: Rust, cargo, Node.js and Tauri are FLOSS.
test: An automated cargo test suite (175 tests, including adversarial safety tests for the deletion guard and command parser) runs on Linux and Windows: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/docs/SAFETY.md
test_most: The engine keeps its safety logic in a pure crate (cwico-core) precisely so that its whole suite - classification, guard, command parsing, plans - runs in CI; the Windows crate tests its host-independent parts.
test_continuous_integration: GitHub Actions runs clippy and tests on Linux and Windows for every push and pull request: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy: CONTRIBUTING.md requires cargo test to pass and adversarial tests for safety changes; SECURITY.md asks reporters for a failing test case: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added: Safety fixes come with tests, e.g. the plan/restore-point visibility fix (PR #55): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/pull/55
tests_documented_added: The test expectations are written in CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/SAFETY.md: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings runs in CI: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
warnings_fixed: Clippy warnings fail CI (-D warnings); main has none.
warnings_strict: Clippy with -D warnings on all targets.
know_secure_design: SECURITY.md lists the design commitments (Critical items can never be removed, catalogue data cannot execute, minimal web-view capabilities, signed updates, recoverable runs) and docs/SAFETY.md the safety model: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/SECURITY.md
know_common_errors: The common errors for an elevated deletion tool are documented with their defences and tests: path traversal into protected locations, command injection through UninstallString, poisoned catalogue data, privilege escalation: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/blob/main/docs/SAFETY.md
crypto_published: Only published algorithms: Ed25519 (minisign) signatures on updates, SHA-256 checksums, TLS for HTTPS.
crypto_call: Update signature checks use tauri-plugin-updater (minisign verification) and HTTPS uses the TLS library of the HTTP client; the project implements no cryptography itself.
crypto_floss: All cryptography comes from FLOSS libraries (Tauri updater, Rust TLS stack).
crypto_keylength: Ed25519 (128-bit security) for update signatures; TLS uses modern defaults.
crypto_weaknesses: No SHA-1, MD5 or other weak algorithm is used for security.
crypto_pfs: HTTPS uses TLS 1.2+/1.3 with ECDHE key exchange.
crypto_random: The program generates no keys or nonces at runtime (signing keys exist only in the release environment).
delivery_mitm: Releases are delivered over HTTPS; installers carry build provenance attestations, SHA256SUMS.txt is published, and updates are only installed if signed with the pinned minisign key.
delivery_unsigned: Update metadata and payloads are fetched over HTTPS and the payload signature is verified against a key pinned in the app, never trusted from the download location.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days: No unpatched medium-or-higher vulnerability is present in the released software. The only open Dependabot alert (GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g, glib < 0.20) is in gtk3 bindings that Tauri pulls in only for Linux targets; the project ships Windows builds only, and cargo tree for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc contains no glib. No fixed glib exists for the gtk3 stack yet.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed: No critical vulnerability has been reported.
no_leaked_credentials: The repository contains no credentials; the updater private key and signing secrets live only in GitHub secrets, and secret scanning with push protection is enabled.
static_analysis: Clippy on every change and GitHub CodeQL code scanning (Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Actions): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsucwico/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities: CodeQL security queries look for common vulnerabilities; clippy includes correctness and suspicious lints.
static_analysis_fixed: No medium or higher severity code vulnerability found by static analysis remains open.
static_analysis_often: Static analysis runs on every push and pull request.
dynamic_analysis: No fuzzing or other dynamic analysis tool is run yet; adversarial unit tests cover the deletion guard and command parser with crafted malicious inputs.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe: The program is written in Rust (safe code) and TypeScript.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions: No dynamic analysis runs yet (see dynamic_analysis).
dynamic_analysis_fixed: No dynamic analysis has been run, so no issue was discovered by it.
